													1340 text Step 1
													1341 heading Wave Movement in the First Medium, Value: 2
														1342 text Wave Movement in the First Medium
													1343 text The wave travels through the first medium (medium 1) with a certain speed (v₁), wavelength (λ₁), and frequency (f). Everything is steady as the wave moves forward.

1338 container 3 of 6
													1339 text 3 of 6
													1340 text Step 2
													1341 heading Encountering the Boundary, Value: 2
														1342 text Encountering the Boundary
													1343 text The wave reaches the boundary between medium 1 and medium 2. This is where the properties of the material change, setting the stage for new behaviors.

1338 container 4 of 6
													1339 text 4 of 6
													1340 text Step 3
													1341 heading Transmission into the Second Medium, Value: 2
														1342 text Transmission into the Second Medium
													1343 text Part of the wave passes into medium 2. In the new medium, the wave now travels at a different speed (v₂) and has a new wavelength (λ₂), but the frequency (f) remains the same as before.

1338 container 5 of 6
													1339 text 5 of 6
													1340 text Step 4
													1341 heading Reflection at the Boundary, Value: 2
														1342 text Reflection at the Boundary
													1343 text Another part of the wave bounces back into medium 1. Depending on the type of boundary, the reflected wave may be inverted (flipped) or upright.
